title: Who is Elon Musk
prompt: Go to en.wikipedia.org and look up Elon Musk. Tell me: (1) his current primary role, (2) his estimated net worth, and (3) the names of the companies he runs or co-founded.
expectedOutput: Agent navigates to en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elon_Musk and returns: primary role (CEO of Tesla / SpaceX / xAI), an estimated net worth in the hundreds of billions USD, and company names including Tesla, SpaceX, X (formerly Twitter), and xAI.

title: Hacker News Top 5 Stories
prompt: Go to news.ycombinator.com. Tell me the exact titles of the top 5 stories on the front page right now.
expectedOutput: Agent navigates to Hacker News (news.ycombinator.com) and returns 5 story titles currently visible on the front page. Exact titles vary by run date — judge should verify the agent visited the page and read live content, not hallucinated titles.

title: NPM lodash Package Info
prompt: Go to npmjs.com and look up the package 'lodash'. Tell me: (1) the latest version number, (2) the weekly download count, and (3) the license type.
expectedOutput: Agent navigates directly to npmjs.com/package/lodash and returns: a version number in the 4.x.x range, a weekly download count in the hundreds of millions, and the MIT license.

title: BTC and ETH Current Prices
prompt: Go to coinmarketcap.com. Find the current price in USD of Bitcoin (BTC) and Ethereum (ETH).
expectedOutput: Agent navigates to coinmarketcap.com and returns two real numeric prices: BTC in the range of tens of thousands USD, ETH in the range of thousands USD. Exact values vary — judge verifies the agent read live numbers from the correct page.

title: Stack Overflow Flatten Array JS
prompt: Go to duckduckgo.com and search for 'how to flatten an array in JavaScript site:stackoverflow.com'. Open the first Stack Overflow result and give me the code snippet from the highest-voted answer.
expectedOutput: Agent navigates to DuckDuckGo, searches the query, opens a Stack Overflow result, and returns actual JavaScript code from the top-voted answer. The code likely involves Array.flat(), reduce(), or concat(). Agent must quote actual code, not just describe it.

title: GitHub React Repo Stars
prompt: Go to github.com/facebook/react. Tell me the approximate number of stars this repository currently has.
expectedOutput: Agent navigates to github.com/facebook/react and returns a star count, e.g., in the hundreds of thousands (like 210k+ stars). Judge verifies it's a realistic number for React.

title: MDN Array Map Documentation
prompt: Go to developer.mozilla.org and search for 'Array.prototype.map()'. Tell me the first sentence of the description for this method.
expectedOutput: Agent navigates to MDN, searches for Array map, and quotes the first sentence of the description which explains that map creates a new array populated with the results of calling a provided function on every element.

title: Python Print Function Docs
prompt: Go to docs.python.org/3/ and search for the built-in 'print' function. What is the default value of the 'sep' parameter?
expectedOutput: Agent navigates to Python 3 documentation, finds the print function, and returns that the default value for 'sep' is a space (' ').

title: Weather via DuckDuckGo
prompt: Go to duckduckgo.com and search for 'weather in New York'. Tell me the current temperature and conditions.
expectedOutput: Agent searches for New York weather on DuckDuckGo and returns a plausible current temperature and weather condition (e.g., cloudy, sunny, raining).

title: Arxiv Search Attention Paper
prompt: Go to arxiv.org and search for 'Attention Is All You Need'. Who is the first author listed on the paper?
expectedOutput: Agent navigates to arxiv.org, searches for the specific paper, and returns 'Ashish Vaswani' as the first author.

title: Tailwind CSS Installation
prompt: Go to tailwindcss.com, navigate to the documentation, and find the installation instructions for using Tailwind CLI. Provide the exact command to install 'tailwindcss' via npm.
expectedOutput: Agent navigates to Tailwind CSS documentation and returns the installation command, which should be something like 'npm install -D tailwindcss' or 'npm install tailwindcss'.

title: React useEffect Docs
prompt: Go to react.dev, search for the 'useEffect' hook. Explain briefly what the dependency array does based on the documentation.
expectedOutput: Agent navigates to React docs, finds useEffect, and explains that the dependency array controls when the effect runs (it skips re-running if dependencies haven't changed).

title: IMDb Top Movie
prompt: Go to imdb.com, find the 'Top 250 Movies' chart. Tell me the title of the #1 rated movie and its release year.
expectedOutput: Agent navigates to IMDb Top 250 and returns 'The Shawshank Redemption' and the year '1994'.

title: Tokyo Timezone
prompt: Go to duckduckgo.com and search for 'Tokyo timezone'. Tell me what timezone Tokyo is in.
expectedOutput: Agent searches DuckDuckGo and returns that Tokyo is in Japan Standard Time (JST) or UTC+9.

title: Capital of Australia
prompt: Go to duckduckgo.com and search for 'capital of Australia'. What is it?
expectedOutput: Agent searches DuckDuckGo and returns 'Canberra' as the capital of Australia.

title: Canada Population Wikipedia
prompt: Go to en.wikipedia.org, look up 'Canada'. What is the estimated population according to the infobox?
expectedOutput: Agent navigates to Wikipedia for Canada and returns a population estimate (typically in the high 30 millions or low 40 millions, e.g., ~40+ million).

title: Latest Ubuntu Release
prompt: Go to ubuntu.com and find the version number of the latest LTS (Long Term Support) release.
expectedOutput: Agent navigates to Ubuntu's site and finds the latest LTS version, such as '24.04 LTS' or whatever is current.

title: Stripe API Create Customer
prompt: Go to docs.stripe.com/api, find the documentation for creating a customer. What are the required parameters, if any, to create a new customer?
expectedOutput: Agent navigates to Stripe API docs, finds the 'Create a customer' endpoint, and correctly states that there are no required parameters (or lists any if the API has changed).

title: Next.js App Router Docs
prompt: Go to nextjs.org/docs and find out what the special file 'layout.tsx' is used for in the App Router.
expectedOutput: Agent navigates to Next.js docs and explains that 'layout.tsx' is used to define a UI that is shared between multiple routes.

title: Vue.js Current Version
prompt: Go to vuejs.org and find the current stable version number of Vue.
expectedOutput: Agent navigates to Vue.js site and returns the current stable version, typically starting with 3.x.
